Independent visitor's guide

# Visit Johannesburg: A Plain Guide to Joburg

Johannesburg is South Africa's biggest city and the place where much of its modern history was made. This guide shows you what to see, where to stay and eat, and how to get around safely.

[See things to do](https://example.com/things-to-do.html)[Getting around](https://example.com/getting-around.html)

## Johannesburg at a Glance

- **1,750 m**above sea level, so days are mild and nights can be cool
- **11**places to visit in this guide
- **67**neighbourhoods worth an afternoon
- **1886**the year gold was found on the Witwatersrand and the city began

## What to See When You Visit Johannesburg

Most visitors come for the history, stay for the food and music, and leave surprised by how green the city is. Here are three ways to spend your time.

### Learn the City's History

Start at the Apartheid Museum, then visit Constitution Hill, a former prison that now houses the Constitutional Court. In Soweto, walk down Vilakazi Street, where Nelson Mandela and Desmond Tutu both lived, and stop at the Hector Pieterson Memorial.

[See all things to do](https://example.com/things-to-do.html).

### Spend an Afternoon in a Neighbourhood

Joburg is a city of distinct areas, each with its own pace. Pick one or two and take your time.

- Braamfontein for its Saturday food market and rooftop bars
- Maboneng for street art, galleries and small shops
- Melville for cafés, bookshops and live music

[Compare the neighbourhoods](https://example.com/neighbourhoods.html).

### Get Outside

Johannesburg is often said to have one of the largest planted urban forests in the world. Walk in the Johannesburg Botanical Garden, picnic at Zoo Lake, or climb the Melville Koppies for a view over the northern suburbs. For a full day out, head to the Cradle of Humankind, a UNESCO World Heritage Site about an hour's drive away.

## Why Visit Johannesburg

Johannesburg is often a stop on the way to somewhere else. These are the reasons to give it a few days of its own.

### History You Can Stand In

- The places where South Africa's freedom struggle happened are open to visit, many with guides who lived through it.
### Food From Everywhere

- Try kota and shisa nyama in Soweto, Ethiopian coffee in the city centre and weekend markets across town.
### A Green City

- Millions of trees, parks and ridges. In spring, jacarandas turn whole streets purple.
### Easy to Reach

- O.R. Tambo is one of Africa's busiest airports, and the Gautrain links it to the city in about 15 minutes.
### Good Weather All Year

- Sunny winters and warm summers with short afternoon storms. Pack a jersey for the evenings.
### Music and Art

- Jazz, amapiano and theatre most nights, and galleries from the city centre to Rosebank.

## How to Plan Your Johannesburg Visit

1. Give the city two or three days. Add a day for the Cradle of Humankind or Pretoria.
2. Stay somewhere central to the Gautrain, such as Rosebank or Sandton, for an easy first trip.
3. Book a guided tour for Soweto and the city centre. Local guides know the stories and the streets.
4. Use ride-hailing apps at night, and keep your phone out of sight on the street.

Read the full [getting around guide](https://example.com/getting-around.html), or follow our [first-day plan](https://example.com/blog/first-day-in-johannesburg.html).

## Questions About Visiting Johannesburg

### When is the best time to visit Johannesburg?

Any time of year works. Summer (October to March) is warm, with short afternoon thunderstorms. Winter (June to August) is dry and sunny, with cold nights. In October and November, jacaranda trees turn many streets purple.

### Which airport serves Johannesburg?

O.R. Tambo International Airport (JNB), about 25 km east of the city centre. The Gautrain runs from the airport to Sandton, and from there to Rosebank and Park Station.

### What currency is used in Johannesburg?

The South African rand (ZAR). Cards are widely accepted. Carry a little cash for markets, tips and car guards.

### How many days do I need in Johannesburg?

Two or three days covers the main museums, Soweto and one or two neighbourhoods. Add a day for the Cradle of Humankind or Pretoria.

### Is Johannesburg safe for visitors?

Most visits pass without trouble if you take sensible care. Use ride-hailing or the Gautrain instead of walking at night, keep phones and bags out of sight, and go with a local guide in areas you do not know.

### Do I need a car in Johannesburg?

No. The Gautrain, ride-hailing apps and guided tours cover most of what visitors want to see. A car helps for day trips out of the city.

More answers on the [FAQ page](https://example.com/faq.html).

## Get the Joburg Weekend Email

One short email on a Thursday with markets, gigs and events for the weekend. No spam, and you can leave at any time.

## Start Planning Your Trip

Pick the places you want to see, check their hours, and plan your days around where you stay.

Things to do

# Things to Do in Johannesburg

These are the places we suggest for a first visit. Hours and prices change, so check each place's own website before you go.

## Museums, Landmarks and Day Trips

### Apartheid Museum

Ormonde

The story of apartheid and the struggle against it, told through film, photographs and personal accounts. Allow at least two to three hours.

- History
- Museums

[Open in Maps: Apartheid Museum](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.2375,28.0103)

### Constitution Hill

Braamfontein

A former prison complex where Nelson Mandela and Mahatma Gandhi were held, now home to the Constitutional Court. Guided tours run through the day.

- History
- Architecture

[Open in Maps: Constitution Hill](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1889,28.0425)

### Vilakazi Street, Soweto

Orlando West, Soweto

The only street in the world where two Nobel Peace Prize winners lived: Nelson Mandela and Archbishop Desmond Tutu. Visit Mandela House and eat at one of the street's restaurants.

- History
- Food

[Open in Maps: Vilakazi Street, Soweto](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.2385,27.9081)

### Hector Pieterson Memorial and Museum

Orlando West, Soweto

A memorial to the students killed in the Soweto uprising of 16 June 1976, a short walk from Vilakazi Street.

- History
- Museums

[Open in Maps: Hector Pieterson Memorial and Museum](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.2381,27.9095)

### Cradle of Humankind

About 50 km northwest of the city

A UNESCO World Heritage Site with some of the world's richest fossil finds of early humans. Visit the Maropeng visitor centre and the Sterkfontein Caves. Plan a full day.

- Day trips
- Science
- Outdoors
- History

[Open in Maps: Cradle of Humankind](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-25.9667,27.6622)

### Johannesburg Botanical Garden

Emmarentia

A large public garden with a rose garden, herb garden and walking paths beside Emmarentia Dam. Free to enter and good for a picnic.

- Outdoors
- Free

[Open in Maps: Johannesburg Botanical Garden](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1597,28.0028)

### Origins Centre

Braamfontein

A museum at Wits University about the origins of modern humans, with a large collection of southern African rock art.

- Science
- Museums
- History
- Arts

[Open in Maps: Origins Centre](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1929,28.0283)

### Liliesleaf

Rivonia

The farm that served as a secret base for the liberation movement in the 1960s. The 1963 police raid here led to the Rivonia Trial.

- History
- Museums

[Open in Maps: Liliesleaf](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.044,28.0546)

### Mandela House

Orlando West, Soweto

Nelson Mandela's family home on Vilakazi Street, now a museum about his life and the Mandela family. Combine it with the Hector Pieterson Memorial nearby.

- History
- Museums

[Open in Maps: Mandela House](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.2385,27.9088)

### Zoo Lake

Parkview and Saxonwold

A public park with a lake, rowing boats, picnic lawns and a fountain, beside the Johannesburg Zoo. The Artists under the Sun art show is held here every month.

- Outdoors
- Family
- Arts

[Open in Maps: Zoo Lake](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1594,28.0305)

### Lion & Safari Park

Near Hartbeespoort, about 40 km north west of the city

A wildlife park about 13 km from Lanseria Airport, with guided and self-drive game drives among lions, cheetahs and giraffes. Plan half a day.

- Day trips
- Family
- Outdoors

[Open in Maps: Lion & Safari Park](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-25.8322,27.8888)

## Tips for Your Visit

- Many museums close on Mondays. Check before you plan your week.
- The Apartheid Museum and Gold Reef City are next to each other, so you can visit both on one day.
- Soweto is best with a local guide. Walking and cycling tours start near Vilakazi Street.
- Leave a full day for the Cradle of Humankind. You need a car or a tour to get there.

Next: [choose a neighbourhood to explore](https://example.com/neighbourhoods.html).

Source: https://example.com/things-to-do.html

Neighbourhoods

# Johannesburg Neighbourhoods to Explore

Joburg is spread out, so it helps to think of it as a set of smaller places. Pick one or two areas a day and travel between them by Gautrain or ride-hailing. The [map on the home page](https://example.com/index.html#map-h) shows where each one sits.

## Where to Go

### Lonehill

A residential suburb in the far north of the city, next to Fourways. We list no visitor sights here yet; Fourways' shopping centres are a short drive away.

[Open in Maps: Lonehill](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.012,28.027)

### Fourways

A busy suburb in the far north of the city, known for large shopping centres and the Montecasino entertainment complex.

Good for: Shopping, theatre and a family day out

[Read the Fourways guide](https://example.com/neighbourhoods/fourways.html) · [Open in Maps: Fourways](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0045,28.0042)

### Glenferness

A residential area in the far north of the city. We list no visitor sights here yet.

### Halfway House

A suburb in Midrand, named for its position roughly halfway between Johannesburg and Pretoria. Mostly offices, homes and shops.

[Open in Maps: Halfway House](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-25.9949,28.1289)

### Glen Austin

A semi-rural area of smallholdings in Midrand, in the far north of the city. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Glen Austin](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-25.9667,28.15)

### Jukskei Park

A residential suburb in the north-west of the city, named after the Jukskei River. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Jukskei Park](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.038,27.981)

### Douglasdale

A residential suburb in the north of the city, between Sandton and Fourways. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Douglasdale](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0389,27.995)

### Olivedale

A residential suburb in the north-west of the city, near Randburg. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Olivedale](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0556,27.9789)

### Randpark Ridge

A residential suburb in the north-west of the city, near Randburg. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Randpark Ridge](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1008,27.9569)

### Ferndale

A residential suburb next to the Randburg town centre, in the north-west of the city. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Ferndale](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0847,27.9894)

### Fairland

A residential suburb in the north-west of the city, near Randburg and Northcliff. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Fairland](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1336,27.9444)

### Robindale

A residential suburb in the north-west of the city, near Randburg. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Robindale](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.115,27.9944)

### Linden

A residential suburb in the north-west of the city with a choice of restaurants and cafés. It is a short drive from Melville and Parkhurst.

Good for: Restaurants and cafés

[Open in Maps: Linden](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1319,27.9933)

### Northcliff

A suburb on and around Northcliff Hill, one of the highest points in the city. Quiet, leafy streets with views over the northern suburbs.

Good for: Views and quiet streets

[Open in Maps: Northcliff](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1311,27.9622)

### Emmarentia

A leafy suburb around Emmarentia Dam, where people walk, run and sail. The Johannesburg Botanical Garden is on the dam's edge.

Good for: Walks, picnics and the Botanical Garden

[Open in Maps: Emmarentia](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1472,27.9958)

### Florida

A suburb in the north-west of the city, close to Roodepoort, built around Florida Lake. Mostly homes and shops.

[Open in Maps: Florida](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1753,27.9233)

### Triomf

Built in the 1950s on the site of Sophiatown, whose residents were forced to leave under apartheid. The name Sophiatown was restored in 2006.

Good for: Apartheid-era history

[Open in Maps: Triomf](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.175,27.9764)

### Melville

A relaxed suburb with a strip of cafés, bookshops and bars along 7th Street, close to the Melville Koppies nature reserve.

Good for: Cafés, live music, a walk on the koppies

[Open in Maps: Melville](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.175,28.008)

### Sandton

The business and shopping heart of northern Johannesburg. Sandton City, Nelson Mandela Square, many hotels and a Gautrain station sit close together.

Good for: Shopping, hotels and a Gautrain base

[Read the Sandton guide](https://example.com/neighbourhoods/sandton.html)

### Bryanston

An established northern suburb with large gardens, a shopping centre and a well-known organic market. A short drive from Sandton.

Good for: A market morning and a quiet meal

[Open in Maps: Bryanston](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0514,28.0281)

### Rivonia

A northern suburb known for Liliesleaf, the farm where anti-apartheid leaders were arrested in 1963 and which is now a museum. Also home to offices and restaurants.

Good for: Liliesleaf and the Rivonia Trial story

[Open in Maps: Rivonia](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0533,28.0594)

### Woodmead

A business district on the N1 north of Sandton, with offices and retail parks. Most visitors pass through on the way to somewhere else.

[Open in Maps: Woodmead](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0433,28.0644)

### Morningside

A residential suburb on the edge of Sandton, with a shopping centre and a number of restaurants. It lies close to the Sandton Gautrain station.

Good for: Restaurants near Sandton

[Open in Maps: Morningside](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0781,28.0644)

### River Club

A small suburb in the Sandton area, in the north of the city. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: River Club](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0744,28.0433)

### Sandown

The part of Sandton around Sandton City and Nelson Mandela Square. Shops, restaurants, hotels and the Sandton Gautrain station are all within walking distance.

Good for: Shopping, hotels and a Gautrain station

[Open in Maps: Sandown](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0919,28.0658)

### Buccleuch

A suburb beside the N1 in the north of the city, with offices and light industry. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Buccleuch](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0553,28.1108)

### Modderfontein

Once the site of a dynamite factory founded in the 1890s. Today it mixes new housing and offices with the Modderfontein Reserve, which has walking trails.

Good for: A walk in the reserve

[Open in Maps: Modderfontein](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0845,28.1669)

### Kelvin

A mostly industrial and commercial suburb on the north-eastern side of the city. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Kelvin](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.075,28.0947)

### Bordeaux

A residential suburb in the north-west of the city, close to Randburg and Craighall. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Bordeaux](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0964,28.0136)

### Parkmore

A suburb just west of Sandton's business centre, with offices, apartment blocks and houses. It is one of the Parks and also counted as part of Sandton.

[Open in Maps: Parkmore](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0953,28.0375)

### Hurlingham

A residential suburb in the Sandton area, in the north of the city. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Hurlingham](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1022,28.0278)

### Sandhurst

One of the city's wealthiest residential suburbs, close to Sandton's centre. Large houses sit behind high walls, so it is a place to drive through rather than visit.

[Open in Maps: Sandhurst](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1078,28.0442)

### Wynberg

A mostly industrial and commercial suburb next to Alexandra, on the north-eastern side of the city. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Wynberg](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1107,28.0835)

### Alexandra

A dense township founded in 1912, just east of Sandton. Nelson Mandela lived here in the 1940s. Go with a local guide.

Good for: Local history, with a guide

[Open in Maps: Alexandra](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1044,28.0989)

### Hyde Park

A wealthy residential suburb best known for Hyde Park Corner, a shopping centre with fashion and homeware shops, restaurants and cafés.

Good for: Shopping and a coffee

[Open in Maps: Hyde Park](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1197,28.0397)

### The Parks

A local name for a group of leafy suburbs north of the city centre whose names start with Park, from Parkhurst and Parkview to Parktown.

Good for: Restaurants, Zoo Lake and old houses

[Read the The Parks guide](https://example.com/neighbourhoods/the-parks.html)

### Parkhurst

A residential suburb known for 4th Avenue, a street of restaurants, cafés and independent shops. One of the Parks.

Good for: Restaurants and browsing on 4th Avenue

[Open in Maps: Parkhurst](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1397,28.0189)

### Parktown North

A residential suburb with a mix of houses and offices, north of Parkwood and Parkhurst. One of the Parks.

[Open in Maps: Parktown North](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1394,28.0303)

### Parkwood

A quiet residential suburb close to Rosebank, between Parkhurst and Parktown North. One of the Parks.

[Open in Maps: Parkwood](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1508,28.0303)

### Parkview

A leafy residential suburb beside Zoo Lake, with a golf course and a small strip of shops and restaurants on Tyrone Avenue. One of the Parks.

Good for: Zoo Lake, picnics and a quiet lunch

[Open in Maps: Parkview](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1642,28.0253)

### Parktown

A suburb on a ridge north of Braamfontein, known for its old houses, many designed by Herbert Baker, and for several large hospitals. One of the Parks.

Good for: Old houses and city views

[Open in Maps: Parktown](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1817,28.0278)

### Illovo

A suburb between Sandton and Rosebank along Oxford Road, with offices, apartment blocks and restaurants.

Good for: Restaurants and a base near both

[Open in Maps: Illovo](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1228,28.0553)

### Melrose

An upmarket suburb best known for Melrose Arch, a walkable precinct of restaurants, shops, offices and hotels.

Good for: A walkable evening out

[Open in Maps: Melrose](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.14,28.0494)

### Rosebank

A compact business and shopping district with its own Gautrain station, a weekend rooftop market and several galleries.

Good for: A first base, shopping, galleries

[Open in Maps: Rosebank](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.146,28.0436)

### Saxonwold

A leafy suburb of old houses and large gardens, home to the Johannesburg Zoo. Zoo Lake is next door.

Good for: The Johannesburg Zoo

[Open in Maps: Saxonwold](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1583,28.0394)

### Orchards

A residential suburb in the north-east of the city. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Orchards](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1547,28.0794)

### Sandringham

A residential suburb in the north-east of the city. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Sandringham](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1494,28.1019)

### Edenvale

A town just east of Johannesburg, in the Ekurhuleni municipality, close to OR Tambo International Airport. Mostly homes, shops and light industry.

[Open in Maps: Edenvale](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1367,28.1511)

### Houghton

A leafy, wealthy suburb where Nelson Mandela lived for many years and died in 2013. The Nelson Mandela Foundation has its offices here. The Mandela home is private.

Good for: Mandela history, from the street

[Open in Maps: Houghton](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1582,28.059)

### Observatory

A residential suburb on a ridge east of the city centre, named after the observatory built there in the early 1900s. Observatory Park is in the suburb.

[Open in Maps: Observatory](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1803,28.0819)

### Bruma

A suburb in the east of the city, centred on Bruma Lake. Mostly shops, offices and apartment blocks.

[Open in Maps: Bruma](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1767,28.1083)

### Bedfordview

A suburb just east of Johannesburg on the N3, in the Ekurhuleni municipality, with the Eastgate shopping centre and a number of restaurants.

Good for: Shopping and restaurants on the way to the airport

[Open in Maps: Bedfordview](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1764,28.1425)

### Braamfontein

A student district next to Wits University. Rooftop bars, galleries, coffee shops and a busy Saturday food market.

Good for: Food markets, nightlife, Constitution Hill

[Read the Braamfontein guide](https://example.com/neighbourhoods/braamfontein.html) · [Open in Maps: Braamfontein](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1929,28.0357)

### Newtown

A cultural quarter in the west of the city centre, home to the Market Theatre and Mary Fitzgerald Square.

Good for: Theatre, music, history

[Open in Maps: Newtown](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.203,28.032)

### Yeoville

A busy, mixed suburb east of Hillbrow. Rockey Street was known for its bars and live music, and the area has long been home to many people from other African countries.

Good for: Local history and a lively street

[Open in Maps: Yeoville](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1839,28.0642)

### Maboneng

A small, walkable precinct on the east side of the city centre, known for street art, galleries, independent shops and restaurants.

Good for: Street art, galleries, weekend markets

[Open in Maps: Maboneng](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.2044,28.0583)

### Kensington

A residential suburb in the east of the city. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Kensington](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1961,28.0969)

### Auckland Park

A suburb in the west of the city, home to the Kingsway campus of the University of Johannesburg and the main studios of the SABC.

[Open in Maps: Auckland Park](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.189,28.0089)

### Riverlea

A residential suburb in the west of the city. We list no visitor sights here yet.

[Open in Maps: Riverlea](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.2117,27.974)

### Hartbeespoort

A dam and holiday town about an hour's drive north-west of the city, in North West province. Popular for weekend trips from Johannesburg.

Good for: A day out of the city

[Open in Maps: Hartbeespoort](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-25.7442,27.8994)

## Where to Stay

For a first visit, stay in Rosebank or Sandton. Both have Gautrain stations, a good choice of hotels and restaurants within a short walk. Melville and Parkhurst have smaller guest houses with a quieter, local feel.

Transport and safety

# Getting Around Johannesburg

Johannesburg is large and spread out. Most visitors use the Gautrain for longer trips and ride-hailing apps for everything else.

## From the Airport

O.R. Tambo International Airport is about 25 km east of the city centre. The Gautrain airport line takes you to Sandton in about 15 minutes. Change at Sandton for Rosebank, Park Station and Pretoria. Ride-hailing cars and metered taxis wait outside the terminals.

## Gautrain

The Gautrain is a fast, clean rapid rail line that links the airport, Sandton, Rosebank, the city centre and Pretoria. Pay with a Gautrain card or a contactless bank card at the gates. Feeder buses run from most stations.

## Ride-Hailing and Taxis

Uber and Bolt both work well in Johannesburg and are the easiest way to travel door to door, especially at night. Check the number plate and the driver's name before you get in.

## Buses and Minibus Taxis

Rea Vaya is a bus rapid transit system with its own lanes, linking Soweto with the city centre. Minibus taxis carry most of the city's commuters. They are cheap but hard to use without local help, so ask a guide or your host first.

## Driving

South Africa drives on the left. A car is useful for day trips, such as the Cradle of Humankind. In the city, expect heavy traffic at rush hour and power cuts that can turn off traffic lights. Treat a dark traffic light as a four-way stop.

## Staying Safe

- Keep your phone, camera and bag out of sight on the street and in the car.
- Use ride-hailing instead of walking after dark, even for short trips.
- Go with a local guide in the city centre and in Soweto.
- Keep car doors locked and windows up at traffic lights.
- In an emergency, call 10111 for the police or 112 from a mobile phone.

Source: https://example.com/getting-around.html


---

Questions and answers

# Johannesburg Travel Questions

Short answers to the questions visitors ask most. If yours is not here, [send it to us](https://example.com/contact.html).

### When is the best time to visit Johannesburg?

Any time of year works. Summer (October to March) is warm, with short afternoon thunderstorms. Winter (June to August) is dry and sunny, with cold nights. In October and November, jacaranda trees turn many streets purple.

### Which airport serves Johannesburg?

O.R. Tambo International Airport (JNB), about 25 km east of the city centre. The Gautrain runs from the airport to Sandton, and from there to Rosebank and Park Station.

### What currency is used in Johannesburg?

The South African rand (ZAR). Cards are widely accepted. Carry a little cash for markets, tips and car guards.

### How many days do I need in Johannesburg?

Two or three days covers the main museums, Soweto and one or two neighbourhoods. Add a day for the Cradle of Humankind or Pretoria.

### Is Johannesburg safe for visitors?

Most visits pass without trouble if you take sensible care. Use ride-hailing or the Gautrain instead of walking at night, keep phones and bags out of sight, and go with a local guide in areas you do not know.

### Do I need a car in Johannesburg?

No. The Gautrain, ride-hailing apps and guided tours cover most of what visitors want to see. A car helps for day trips out of the city.

Source: https://example.com/faq.html

# About Visit Joburg

Visit Joburg is an independent guide to Johannesburg for visitors. We want to help people see more of the city, with clear advice in plain words.

## What We Include

We list places we would send a friend to on their first visit. Nobody pays to be included. When we link to a business, it is because we think it is useful, and we do not earn a fee for it.

## Keeping It Accurate

Opening hours, prices and transport change often, so we do not list them. Each listing links to a map, and we ask you to check details with the place itself before you go. Each page shows the date we last reviewed it.

## Not an Official Body

Visit Joburg is not linked to the City of Johannesburg, the Gauteng Tourism Authority or South African Tourism.

## Suggest a Change

If something is wrong or missing, [tell us](https://example.com/contact.html). We read every message.

# Accessibility Statement

We aim to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA on every page of this site.

## What We Do

- One main heading per page and headings in order.
- Landmarks for the header, navigation, main content and footer, and a skip link as the first thing in the tab order.
- Text contrast of at least 4.5 to 1 in both light and dark colour schemes.
- Visible focus on every link and control, and touch targets of at least 44 by 44 pixels.
- A text alternative for every image that carries meaning.
- Form fields with visible labels.
- No movement unless you ask for it, and support for reduced motion and forced colours.
- A menu that works with the keyboard. The Escape key closes it.

## How We Check

Every build runs automated checks on headings, images, links, forms and colour contrast. Before each release we also test with Lighthouse, axe and a screen reader.

Itinerary

# How to Spend Your First Day in Johannesburg

By the Visit Joburg team. Published 11 November 2026.

A first day in Johannesburg can feel like a lot. This plan keeps travel short, puts the history first and ends somewhere you can relax. It works best with a ride-hailing app or a booked driver.

## Morning: The Apartheid Museum

Arrive when the museum opens. The exhibits move from the start of apartheid to the first democratic election in 1994, and they take time to read and watch. Two to three hours is about right. Your entry ticket tells you which entrance to use, based on a racial category, so the visit starts with how apartheid divided people.

## Lunch: Vilakazi Street, Soweto

Take a short ride west to Soweto. Vilakazi Street has several restaurants serving South African food, from braaied meat to pap and chakalaka. After lunch, visit Mandela House, then walk to the Hector Pieterson Memorial. A local guide adds the stories you will not find on the signs.

## Afternoon: Constitution Hill

Head back towards the city centre for Constitution Hill. The old prison cells sit next to the Constitutional Court, which was built partly from the bricks of the demolished awaiting-trial block. Join a guided tour if you can.

## Evening: Braamfontein or Maboneng

Constitution Hill sits on the edge of Braamfontein, so you can end the day at a rooftop bar or a restaurant a few minutes away. If you prefer street art and small galleries, take a short ride to Maboneng instead. Either way, book your ride home rather than walking after dark.

### Braamfontein at a Glance

A student district next to Wits University. Rooftop bars, galleries, coffee shops and a busy Saturday food market.

**Part of the city**

Central

**Good for**

History, Food, Nightlife, Arts, Markets

**Places here**

- [Constitution Hill](https://example.com/things-to-do.html#constitution-hill)
- [Origins Centre](https://example.com/things-to-do.html#origins-centre)

[Read the Braamfontein guide](https://example.com/neighbourhoods/braamfontein.html) · [Open in Maps: Braamfontein](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1929,28.0357)

## Before You Go

- Check opening days. Many museums close on Mondays.
- Carry a little cash for tips and small purchases in Soweto.
- Wear comfortable shoes and bring a jersey for the evening.

Want more ideas? See all [things to do in Johannesburg](https://example.com/things-to-do.html).

Source: https://example.com/blog/first-day-in-johannesburg.html

Neighbourhood guide

# Braamfontein

Braamfontein sits just north of the city centre, between the University of the Witwatersrand and Constitution Hill. It is young, busy and easy to explore on foot by day.

## Braamfontein at a Glance

A student district next to Wits University. Rooftop bars, galleries, coffee shops and a busy Saturday food market.

**Part of the city**

Central

**Good for**

History, Food, Nightlife, Arts, Markets

**Places here**

- [Constitution Hill](https://example.com/things-to-do.html#constitution-hill)
- [Origins Centre](https://example.com/things-to-do.html#origins-centre)

[Open in Maps: Braamfontein](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1929,28.0357)

## What to Do

Start at Constitution Hill, the former prison that is now home to the Constitutional Court. Then walk west into the main streets of Braamfontein for coffee, galleries and shops run by local designers.

On Saturdays, a food market in Juta Street draws a big crowd. Arrive before midday for the best choice. In the evening, rooftop bars and restaurants fill up with students and people who work nearby.

## Getting There

Braamfontein is a short ride-hailing trip from Rosebank or the city centre. Park Station, on the Gautrain line, is about a 15-minute walk away. The Nelson Mandela Bridge links Braamfontein with Newtown to the south.

## Staying Safe

The main streets are busy and well used in the day. After dark, use ride-hailing rather than walking between venues, and keep your phone out of sight on the street.

See more [neighbourhoods](https://example.com/neighbourhoods.html) or the full list of [things to do](https://example.com/things-to-do.html).

Source: https://example.com/neighbourhoods/braamfontein.html

Neighbourhood guide

# Fourways

Fourways is a large suburb in the far north of Johannesburg. Most visitors come for its shopping centres and for Montecasino, an entertainment complex with theatres, restaurants and a casino.

## Fourways at a Glance

A busy suburb in the far north of the city, known for large shopping centres and the Montecasino entertainment complex.

**Part of the city**

Far North and Midrand

**Good for**

Shopping, Entertainment, Family

**Places here**

- Cedar Square
- Fourways Mall
- Montecasino

[Open in Maps: Fourways](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0045,28.0042)

## What to Do

Montecasino is built to look like an Italian village, with streets, squares and restaurants under one roof. It has theatres that stage musicals and shows, cinemas and a bird garden that suits a family outing.

Fourways Mall is one of the largest shopping centres in South Africa. Cedar Square is smaller and quicker to get around. Both have restaurants for a meal between shops.

## Getting There

Fourways has no Gautrain station, so most visitors arrive by car or ride-hailing. From Sandton, the trip takes about 20 to 40 minutes, depending on traffic. Allow extra time at rush hour.

## Nearby

Lonehill, Dainfern and Kyalami are close by. Further south, Bryanston and Sandton have more hotels and restaurants.

See more [neighbourhoods](https://example.com/neighbourhoods.html) or the full list of [things to do](https://example.com/things-to-do.html).

Source: https://example.com/neighbourhoods/fourways.html

Neighbourhood guide

# Sandton

Sandton is the business and shopping district of northern Johannesburg. It is the part of the city with the most hotels, offices and large shopping centres, and it is the easiest place to reach from the airport by train.

## Sandton at a Glance

The business and shopping heart of northern Johannesburg. Sandton City, Nelson Mandela Square, many hotels and a Gautrain station sit close together.

**Part of the city**

Sandton, Rosebank and North Central

**Good for**

Shopping, Food

## What to Do

Most visitors start at Sandton City, a large shopping centre opened in 1973. A walkway leads from it to Nelson Mandela Square, where a bronze statue of Nelson Mandela stands among restaurants and cafés. Both are easy to reach on foot from the Sandton Gautrain station.

Sandton is a shopping and dining area more than a sightseeing one. For museums and history, plan day trips to [Braamfontein](https://example.com/neighbourhoods/braamfontein.html) or the Apartheid Museum, listed on the [things to do](https://example.com/things-to-do.html) page.

People use "Sandton" for a wider group of suburbs than the business district. The ones below are the most useful to know. Areas around the centre are quiet and residential, so expect to travel by car or ride-hailing.

## Sandown

This is the part of Sandton most people mean when they say they are staying in Sandton.

### Sandown at a Glance

The part of Sandton around Sandton City and Nelson Mandela Square. Shops, restaurants, hotels and the Sandton Gautrain station are all within walking distance.

**Part of the city**

Sandton, Rosebank and North Central

**Good for**

Shopping, Food, Nightlife

**Places here**

- Nelson Mandela Square
- Sandton City

[Open in Maps: Sandown](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0919,28.0658)

## Hyde Park

### Hyde Park at a Glance

A wealthy residential suburb best known for Hyde Park Corner, a shopping centre with fashion and homeware shops, restaurants and cafés.

**Part of the city**

Sandton, Rosebank and North Central

**Good for**

Shopping

[Open in Maps: Hyde Park](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1197,28.0397)

## Bryanston

### Bryanston at a Glance

An established northern suburb with large gardens, a shopping centre and a well-known organic market. A short drive from Sandton.

**Part of the city**

Sandton, Rosebank and North Central

**Good for**

Markets, Food

[Open in Maps: Bryanston](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.0514,28.0281)

## Sandhurst

### Sandhurst at a Glance

One of the city's wealthiest residential suburbs, close to Sandton's centre. Large houses sit behind high walls, so it is a place to drive through rather than visit.

**Part of the city**

Sandton, Rosebank and North Central

[Open in Maps: Sandhurst](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1078,28.0442)

## Getting There

The Gautrain runs from OR Tambo International Airport to Sandton station in about 15 minutes. From there, Rosebank is one stop away and Park Station, in the city centre, is a longer ride on the same line. Check the current timetable and fares on the Gautrain website before you travel.

Outside the centre, distances are larger than they look on a map. Use ride-hailing or a hotel transfer, and allow extra time at rush hour.

## Staying Safe

The area around Sandton City and Nelson Mandela Square is busy and well guarded in the day. In the evening, book a ride-hailing car to the door rather than walking between venues, and keep phones and bags out of sight on the street.

See more [neighbourhoods](https://example.com/neighbourhoods.html) or the full list of [things to do](https://example.com/things-to-do.html).

Source: https://example.com/neighbourhoods/sandton.html

Neighbourhood guide

# The Parks

"The Parks" is a local name for a group of suburbs north of the city centre whose names start with Park: Parkhurst, Parkview, Parktown, Parkwood, Parktown North and Parkmore. They are leafy, mostly residential and close to Rosebank.

## The Parks at a Glance

A local name for a group of leafy suburbs north of the city centre whose names start with Park, from Parkhurst and Parkview to Parktown.

**Part of the city**

Sandton, Rosebank and North Central

**Good for**

Food, Outdoors

## What to Do

Each suburb has a different character, so pick one or two for a day. Parkhurst has a street of restaurants and shops, Parkview has Zoo Lake, and Parktown has some of the city's oldest houses.

## Parkhurst

Walk 4th Avenue for coffee, lunch and independent shops. It is the busiest of the Parks in the evenings.

### Parkhurst at a Glance

A residential suburb known for 4th Avenue, a street of restaurants, cafés and independent shops. One of the Parks.

**Part of the city**

Sandton, Rosebank and North Central

**Good for**

Food, Shopping

[Open in Maps: Parkhurst](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1397,28.0189)

## Parkview

Zoo Lake is the main draw. Bring a picnic, hire a rowing boat, or walk around the lake. A small strip of restaurants on Tyrone Avenue is a short drive away.

### Parkview at a Glance

A leafy residential suburb beside Zoo Lake, with a golf course and a small strip of shops and restaurants on Tyrone Avenue. One of the Parks.

**Part of the city**

Sandton, Rosebank and North Central

**Good for**

Outdoors, Food, Family

**Places here**

- [Zoo Lake](https://example.com/things-to-do.html#zoo-lake)

[Open in Maps: Parkview](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1642,28.0253)

## Parktown

Parktown sits on a ridge, and many of its old houses were designed by the architect Herbert Baker. Most are private, so look from the street and respect residents. The area also has several large hospitals, so traffic is heavy on weekdays.

### Parktown at a Glance

A suburb on a ridge north of Braamfontein, known for its old houses, many designed by Herbert Baker, and for several large hospitals. One of the Parks.

**Part of the city**

Sandton, Rosebank and North Central

[Open in Maps: Parktown](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=-26.1817,28.0278)

## Parkwood, Parktown North and Parkmore

These three are mostly homes and offices. Parkwood and Parktown North lie close to Rosebank, which makes them handy places to stay. Parkmore is also counted as part of [Sandton](https://example.com/neighbourhoods/sandton.html).

## Getting There

The Parks do not have their own Gautrain stations. Use Rosebank station and take a short ride-hailing trip, or travel by car. Distances between the suburbs are short, but the roads are busy at rush hour.

## Staying Safe

The streets are quiet and the main shopping streets are busy. Keep valuables out of sight, park in guarded or well-lit places, and use ride-hailing after dark.
